The core insight is that behavior cannot be reduced to simple stimulus-response mappings. Instead, it involves a support-dependent mechanism where responses are not merely triggered by stimuli but require an underlying support structure. This implies a stochastic framework where P(R|S,T) governs behavior, with T representing the necessary background condition for R to occur. The molar level of behavior emerges from aggregating unitary behaviors, suggesting a hierarchical Bayesian structure where higher-level models must account for lower-level dependencies. Conditioned reflexes, while useful, are insufficient alone due to their inherent limitations in capturing complex interactions. Thus, the system must incorporate both probabilistic inference (GSI) and multi-agent simulation (GSE) to accurately model behavior.
